title: Paloma and the Trail
premise: Petra Dunmore, a storm chaser deep in debt to a cheerful, ruthless lending syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover a vanished government survey team's equipment along the Kessume River. With her estranged brother-in-loyalty Teo and a defector cartographer named Ilsa, she follows the river upstream into a valley the state has erased from every map, discovering the surveyors didn't vanish — they were silenced after finding a buried water-diversion scheme that starves downstream towns to enrich the syndicate's backers. Pursued by both the syndicate's collectors and government wardens, Petra must choose between selling the evidence to clear her debts and broadcasting it to save the valley. In the end she releases the data publicly at the cost of the bounty on her head, pays her debts in a different currency — testimony — and walks out of the valley alive, hunted but free.
about_author: Rosalind Joubert is the pen name of a former river-guide turned novelist who once spent a season mapping tributaries in a valley that no longer appears on official maps. She writes adventure fiction about people who survive by refusing to stop moving.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Chasing a storm across the flats to earn salvage fees, Petra calculates how many more runs she needs to clear her debt to the Meridian Optimists, whose collector, Voss, delivers a smiling ultimatum. Teo warns her to run; she takes a contract instead: recover a vanished survey team's gear. Emotional beat: the exhausting math of survival.

chapters.title: Gear With No Owners
chapters.summary: Petra and Teo reach the abandoned survey camp — tents zipped, meals half-eaten, instruments still logging — and no tracks leading away. Teo's POV reveals his private fear that Petra is trading her life for pride. They find a torn field journal referencing a 'source that isn't on the map.' Emotional beat: wrongness that curdles curiosity into dread.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Jumped
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They intercept Ilsa, the survey team's cartographer, who fled rather than be silenced; she carries the journal's missing pages showing the Kessume's true source lies inside a closed military reserve. Voss's collectors arrive behind them. A night chase downriver forces an uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: trust extended under a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The trio abandons roads and follows the river on foot through canyon country, Ilsa teaching Petra how to read water as the surveyors did. They find the second survey camp — burned, with a warden's insignia in the ash. Emotional beat: the slow bonding of people who owe each other nothing and give everything.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Guard
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Captured by a warden patrol, Petra bargains her way loose by pretending to accept a deal: the wardens want the journal pages destroyed and offer to clear her debts. She learns the diversion scheme is sanctioned at the highest level. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of rescue.

chapters.title: The Town That Drinks Last
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Detouring downstream, they witness a village's wells failing and hear elders describe the river 'changing its mind' two years ago — the exact date the diversion began. Teo confronts Petra about the warden deal. Emotional beat: abstract injustice made painfully, thirstily specific.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Voss catches them alone and offers a clean trade: the pages for Petra's debt, no violence, everyone walks. Teo, secretly, nearly takes a side deal to save her. Petra refuses — not from heroism, but because she finally understands what the pages cost the surveyors. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by a fair-sounding devil.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The trio breaches the reserve and reaches the source: a massive hidden intake and pumping station diverting the river, staffed by contractors who were the surveyors' killers. Ilsa photographs everything; an alarm betrays them. A running firefight through the intake tunnels. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fury at the scale of the theft.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax. Cornered at a ridge relay station, Petra must choose between Voss's final offer — debt erased, Ilsa surrendered — and transmitting the evidence to every downstream news outlet. She broadcasts it, destroying her own leverage. Wardens and collectors converge as the story goes public in real time, making her too famous to quietly kill. Emotional beat: the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Walking Out
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, resolution. The diversion is exposed; hearings begin; Voss's syndicate fractures under scrutiny. Petra's debts are settled by her testimony, not her money. Teo and Ilsa part ways with her at the trailhead — Petra, still hunted by the men who lost everything, keeps moving, but now by choice. Emotional beat: freedom that costs everything and is worth it.
